title: Deconstructing Sunlight - A Community Enterprise
summary: A memoir of a sixty year career in solar physics.

AI.tldr: A first-person retrospective covering six decades of research in solar physics.
AI.motivation: To document and reflect on a long career in solar physics, presumably sharing insights, historical context, and lessons learned.
AI.method: A memoir-style narrative based on personal experience and recollection rather than a formal scientific methodology.
AI.result: No specific scientific results are reported; the output is the memoir itself.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes with reflections on the author's career in solar physics, offering a historical perspective spanning sixty years.

title: Solar-Cycle Modulation and Photospheric Magnetic Control of Turbulence in the Young Solar Wind
summary: The solar wind is an outflow of solar plasma that expands from the corona to fill the heliosphere. Its turbulence provides a pathway for non-adiabatic heating and acceleration, and is therefore central to understanding the thermodynamic and magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) evolution of the young solar wind. However, the variation of its turbulence properties over the solar activity cycle and the connection of these properties to solar source regions remains incompletely understood. Here we analyze observations from 25 solar orbits of NASA's Parker Solar Probe (PSP) mission, in combination with a global MHD model, photospheric magnetograms, and extreme ultraviolet maps of the low corona, to investigate the solar-cycle dependence and the solar sources of turbulence in the very inner heliosphere. The observations reveal pronounced solar-activity variation in fluctuation amplitude, cross helicity, and related turbulence properties. By tracing PSP-connected magnetic flux tubes to their solar sources, we demonstrate that high turbulent-energy intervals are preferentially connected to coronal-hole sources with unipolar magnetic topology, whereas low turbulent-energy intervals are associated with multipolar topology and active-region environments. Our study combines in-situ measurements with numerical modeling and remote sensing observations to reveal how solar-cycle-dependent source structure determines turbulence variability and plasma heating in the young solar wind.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes 25 Parker Solar Probe orbits combined with global MHD modeling, photospheric magnetograms, and EUV observations to show that solar-wind turbulence properties in the inner heliosphere vary strongly with the solar cycle, and that high turbulent energy is preferentially connected to unipolar coronal-hole sources while low turbulent energy is linked to multipolar active-region environments.
AI.motivation: The solar wind's turbulence drives non-adiabatic heating and acceleration, but its variation over the solar activity cycle and its connection to solar source regions remain incompletely understood.
AI.method: Combines in-situ observations from 25 PSP solar orbits with a global MHD model, photospheric magnetograms, and EUV maps of the low corona. PSP-connected magnetic flux tubes are traced back to their solar source regions to correlate turbulence properties with source topology.
AI.result: Pronounced solar-activity variation is observed in fluctuation amplitude, cross helicity, and related turbulence properties. High turbulent-energy intervals are preferentially connected to coronal-hole sources with unipolar magnetic topology, whereas low turbulent-energy intervals are associated with multipolar topology and active-region environments.
AI.conclusion: Solar-cycle-dependent source structure determines turbulence variability and plasma heating in the young solar wind, demonstrating that the source-region topology governs turbulence properties in the inner heliosphere.

title: Diameters and Temperatures VII: High-angular resolution measurements of Solar-type stars with the CHARA Array
comment: 20 pages, submitted to the Open Journal for Astrophysics (OJA)
summary: We present interferometric measurements of angular diameters for 27 nearby solar-type stars obtained with the Precision Astronomical Visible Observations (PAVO) beam combiner at the CHARA Array. The sample spans a broad range of metallicities, includes several known exoplanet hosts, and covers evolutionary stages from the zero-age main sequence to mildly evolved subgiants. Uniform-disk and limb-darkened angular diameters were measured for each target and combined with bolometric fluxes and Gaia parallaxes to determine precise, model-independent stellar radii, effective temperatures, and luminosities. We achieve typical uncertainties of $\sim1$\% in radius and $\sim1.5$\% in effective temperature. Comparisons with multiple stellar evolutionary model grids yield mass and age estimates and enable assessment of grid-to-grid systematics, highlighting sensitivities to abundances, evolutionary stage, and proximity to grid boundaries. Our results provide empirical benchmarks for testing stellar evolutionary theory, refining surface brightness-color relations, and improving the characterization of exoplanet host stars.

AI.tldr: The paper presents interferometric angular diameter measurements for 27 nearby solar-type stars using the PAVO beam combiner at the CHARA Array, covering a wide range of metallicities and evolutionary stages. These measurements are combined with bolometric fluxes and Gaia parallaxes to derive precise, model-independent stellar radii, effective temperatures, and luminosities, with typical uncertainties of ~1% in radius and ~1.5% in effective temperature. The results enable stellar evolutionary model comparisons and provide empirical benchmarks for stellar theory and exoplanet host characterization.
AI.motivation: To provide precise, model-independent empirical measurements of fundamental stellar parameters (radius, temperature, luminosity) for nearby solar-type stars across a wide range of metallicities and evolutionary stages, which serve as benchmarks for testing stellar evolutionary theory, refining surface brightness-color relations, and improving exoplanet host star characterization.
AI.method: The authors used the Precision Astronomical Visible Observations (PAVO) beam combiner at the CHARA Array to perform interferometric measurements of angular diameters for 27 solar-type stars. Uniform-disk and limb-darkened angular diameters were derived for each target. These were combined with bolometric fluxes and Gaia parallaxes to compute model-independent stellar radii, effective temperatures, and luminosities. Comparisons with multiple stellar evolutionary model grids provided mass and age estimates and allowed assessment of grid-to-grid systematic uncertainties.
AI.result: The study achieved typical uncertainties of ~1% in stellar radius and ~1.5% in effective temperature. Comparisons across multiple evolutionary model grids revealed sensitivities to abundances, evolutionary stage, and proximity to grid boundaries, enabling assessment of grid-to-grid systematics in mass and age estimates.
AI.conclusion: The measurements provide high-precision empirical benchmarks for testing stellar evolutionary theory, refining surface brightness-color relations, and improving the characterization of exoplanet host stars, with quantified grid-to-grid systematics for stellar mass and age determinations.

title: Numerous bow shocks in the outer Helix Nebula
summary: Near the end of their lives, low- and intermediate-mass stars expel metal-enriched material in winds and outflows, ultimately producing planetary nebulae (PNe). The ejected material is expected to fragment and mix into the interstellar medium (ISM), but this final assimilation step has been difficult to observe directly. Here we report evidence for this process in the form of twenty-two bow shocks in the eastern outskirts of the Helix Nebula, detected in H$α$ emission with the partially completed MOTHRA telescope. Unlike the large-scale wind-ISM bow shocks commonly observed around evolved stars, the shocks are compact and associated with individual clumps of gas. Going outward from the central star, the radius of curvature $R_c$ decreases by a factor of ~100 over the radial range r=0.4-1.4 pc. This is accompanied by a morphological transition from thin, well-defined bows to fuzzy, patchy structures. We interpret these changes as progressive stripping and fragmentation of AGB-shell remnants as they interact with the ISM. The slope of the observed $R_c - r$ relation implies a loss of fragment coherence on a timescale of ~10,000 yr, providing a rare direct constraint on the time-scale for disruption and entrainment of fragmented stellar ejecta into the ISM.

AI.tldr: The paper reports the first direct observational evidence of the final stage of stellar ejecta assimilation into the interstellar medium, found as 22 compact bow shocks in the eastern outskirts of the Helix Nebula. These shocks, detected in Hα emission with the MOTHRA telescope, show radius of curvature decreasing ~100× over 0.4–1.4 pc and a morphological transition, implying fragmentation and mixing of AGB-shell remnants on a timescale of ~10,000 yr.
AI.motivation: Low- and intermediate-mass stars eject metal-enriched material near the end of their lives, producing planetary nebulae. While the ejected material is expected to fragment and mix into the ISM, this final assimilation step has been difficult to observe directly. The paper aims to provide direct observational evidence for this process.
AI.method: The authors detected 22 bow shocks in the eastern outskirts of the Helix Nebula using Hα emission observations with the partially completed MOTHRA telescope. They analyzed the radius of curvature (Rc) as a function of radial distance from the central star and examined morphological characteristics of the shocks.
AI.result: The bow shocks are compact, associated with individual gas clumps, and distinct from large-scale wind-ISM bow shocks. The radius of curvature decreases by ~100× over r = 0.4–1.4 pc, accompanied by a transition from thin, well-defined bows to fuzzy, patchy structures. The Rc–r slope implies a loss of fragment coherence on a timescale of ~10,000 yr.
AI.conclusion: The observations provide the first direct constraint on the timescale for disruption and entrainment of fragmented stellar ejecta into the ISM (~10,000 yr), illuminating the progressive stripping and fragmentation of AGB-shell remnants as they interact with the ISM.

title: A Helium-shell Burning Blue Horizontal Branch Star Produced from Common Envelope Evolution
summary: Observationally, blue horizontal branch (BHB) stars are defined as hot stars occupying a characteristic region between the extreme blue horizontal branch and RR Lyrae variables in the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram. Most of them are interpreted as stripped core-helium-burning stars, but the role of binary interaction in their formation remains unclear. Here, we report the discovery of a metal-rich BHB star in a 0.82628-day binary system (\Feige 64) comprising a $0.35\pm0.03\,M_{\odot}$ BHB star and a likely $1.26\pm0.17\,M_{\odot}$ white dwarf (WD). The BHB star has an effective temperature of $15{,}524\pm310$\, K and a luminosity of $39.7\pm4.1\,L_{\odot}$. Stellar evolution modelling indicates that it is a helium-shell-burning star produced through the common-envelope channel, retaining a hydrogen-rich envelope that is more massive than previously thought for low-mass stars. This finding provides direct evidence for binary interaction in the formation of BHB stars, offering a fresh perspective on interpreting this emerging population.

AI.tldr: The paper reports the discovery of Feige 64, a metal-rich blue horizontal branch (BHB) star in a 0.826-day binary system, comprising a 0.35 M⊙ BHB star and a likely white dwarf companion. This is the first direct evidence that binary interaction—specifically a common-envelope channel—can form BHB stars, with the BHB star being a helium-shell-burning star retaining a more massive hydrogen-rich envelope than previously expected for low-mass stars.
AI.motivation: BHB stars are observationally defined as hot stars between the extreme blue horizontal branch and RR Lyrae variables in the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram. While most are interpreted as stripped core-helium-burning stars, the role of binary interaction in their formation has remained unclear, motivating the investigation of this binary system.
AI.method: The authors conducted a discovery and characterization of the Feige 64 binary system using stellar evolution modelling, determining stellar parameters: a 0.35±0.03 M⊙ BHB star with effective temperature 15,524±310 K and luminosity 39.7±4.1 L⊙, alongside a 1.26±0.17 M⊙ white dwarf, in a 0.82628-day orbit.
AI.result: Stellar evolution modelling shows the BHB star is a helium-shell-burning star formed through the common-envelope channel, retaining a hydrogen-rich envelope more massive than previously thought for low-mass stars. This provides direct observational evidence for binary interaction in BHB star formation.
AI.conclusion: The discovery of Feige 64 demonstrates that binary interaction, specifically via the common-envelope channel, can produce BHB stars, offering a fresh perspective on interpreting this emerging population of stars.

title: Disco in the Dust: Reflected light at the bow shock around Betelgeuse's companion explains its observed luminosity
comment: 4 figures, 1 table, submitting to AAS Journals. Comments welcome!
summary: Recent detections of $α$ Orionis B, the putative companion to Betelgeuse, have been reported using multiple instruments and techniques. These include, most recently, a $>6σ$ detection using VLT/SPHERE reported by Montarges+2026. The authors infer a bright companion ($\sim10^{-3}\times$ Betelgeuse's luminosity) with a mass of $2-3\,M_\odot$ and $T_\text{eff}\approx10-12{,}000$\,K, loosely consistent with the uppermost bounds of Howell+2025's recent mass estimate from speckle-imaging. However, it is in tension by a factor of two with the reported mass-exclusion limits via non-detection from a recent HST far-UV campaign (Goldberg+2025). While mass identification from isochrone-fitting (conducted in all cases) is prone to uncertainty, the restrictive HST upper limit on FUV flux precludes the hot, blue emission of a $\gtrsim2\,M_\odot$ main-sequence star. This discrepancy is reconciled by the following hypothesis: these detections observe the reflection of Betelgeuse's own luminosity scattered off the companion's bow shock and wake as it traverses the dusty circumstellar medium. To evaluate the feasibility of this scenario, we draw from custom, filter-specific stellar models computed with MESA, as well as Athena++ simulations of the companion's bow shock in idealized conditions. Importantly, the expansive bow shock from a stellar-mass object necessarily subtends a sizable portion of Betelgeuse's outgoing flux. We find that optical luminosity ratios of $\sim10^{-3}-10^{-4}$ are straightforward to resolve within reasonable assumptions about the companion mass and circumstellar dust, and disfavor a hot $3\,M_\odot$ companion. We thereby reconcile competing mass hypotheses across observational campaigns through proper attribution of the observed brightness, motivating future multi-wavelength campaigns to further characterize this enigmatic system.

AI.tldr: Recent detections of a putative companion to Betelgeuse (α Orionis B) conflict with HST far-UV non-detection mass limits. The authors propose that the observed signal is not a hot main-sequence star but rather the reflection of Betelgeuse's own light scattered off the companion's bow shock and wake in the dusty circumstellar medium, reconciling the discrepant mass estimates.
AI.motivation: The reported detections of α Orionis B using VLT/SPHERE (a >6σ signal) and other instruments imply a bright companion with mass 2–3 M☉ and Teff ~10–12,000 K, but this is in tension with HST far-UV non-detection upper limits that preclude such a hot, massive main-sequence companion. The paper aims to resolve this astrophysical discrepancy.
AI.method: The authors construct custom, filter-specific stellar models with MESA and perform Athena++ hydrodynamic simulations of the companion's bow shock under idealized conditions. They assess whether scattered light from Betelgeuse reflected off the bow shock and wake can account for the detected signal.
AI.result: The expansive bow shock from a stellar-mass companion subtends a large fraction of Betelgeuse's outgoing flux, yielding optical luminosity ratios of ~10⁻³–10⁻⁴ that are consistent with observations under reasonable assumptions about companion mass and dust properties. This disfavors a hot 3 M☉ companion and reconciles the competing mass hypotheses.
AI.conclusion: The observed signal of α Orionis B is most likely reflected/scattered Betelgeuse light off the companion's bow shock and wake, rather than direct emission from a hot main-sequence star. This reconciles the mass-exclusion limits from HST with positive detections, and motivates future multi-wavelength observations to further constrain the system.

title: Statistics of Solar Filament Mass based on CHASE Sun-as-a-star Spectroscopic Observations
comment: 11 pages, 5 figures. Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal Letters
summary: Filaments are cool and dense plasmas suspended in the hot corona of the Sun and other stars. Accurately estimating their masses is of great significance for understanding subsequent eruptions and induced space weather effects, but it remains hindered by their intrinsic geometric uncertainties, particularly in spatially unresolved stellar observations. To test and calibrate the methods for estimating the masses of stellar filaments, we conduct a statistical Sun-as-a-star analysis of solar filaments, utilizing full-disk H$α$ spectroscopic observations from the Chinese H$α$ Solar Explorer (CHASE). A total of 1346 filaments, covering a period from January 2024 to October 2025, are identified via a machine-learning segmentation model. We construct their virtual sun-as-a-star spectra by spatially integrating the filament regions and then obtain their optical parameters by cloud-model fitting. Upon correcting projection effects, we establish a representative three-dimensional morphological scaling of length, apparent width, and line-of-sight depth ($L:W_{\rm app}:D_{\rm LOS} \approx 4.5:1:1.7$), with a median filament depth of about 8000 km. Interestingly, the Sun-as-a-star estimated mass shows high consistency with the resolved intrinsic mass across the full sample, with a log-space regression slope of 1.07. As the first large-sample Sun-as-a-star study of solar filaments, our results provide empirical constraints on filament geometries and masses, offering a critical reference for estimating stellar filament masses based on H$α$ spectroscopy.

AI.tldr: This paper conducts the first large-sample Sun-as-a-star analysis of 1,346 solar filaments using CHASE full-disk Hα spectra, establishing a representative 3D morphological scaling (L:W:D ≈ 4.5:1:1.7) and demonstrating that Sun-as-a-star estimated filament masses closely match resolved intrinsic masses.
AI.motivation: Accurately estimating stellar filament masses is critical for understanding eruptions and space weather, but is hindered by geometric uncertainties, especially for spatially unresolved stellar observations. This work aims to test and calibrate methods for estimating stellar filament masses using solar filaments as a proxy.
AI.method: Using full-disk Hα spectroscopic observations from CHASE, 1,346 filaments (Jan 2024–Oct 2025) are identified via machine-learning segmentation. Virtual sun-as-a-star spectra are constructed by spatially integrating filament regions, and optical parameters are obtained via cloud-model fitting. Projection effects are corrected to establish 3D morphological scaling relationships.
AI.result: A representative morphological scaling of length:apparent width:line-of-sight depth ≈ 4.5:1:1.7 is established with a median filament depth of ~8,000 km. Sun-as-a-star estimated masses show high consistency with resolved intrinsic masses across the full sample, with a log-space regression slope of 1.07.
AI.conclusion: This first large-sample Sun-as-a-star study provides empirical constraints on filament geometries and masses, offering a critical reference for estimating stellar filament masses from Hα spectroscopy.

title: Results from the first spectropolarimetric survey of $γ$ Dor pulsators
comment: 26 pages, 11 figures, 2 tables. Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary:
Context. Magnetic fields can have an important influence on stellar structure and evolution. In intermediate-mass (A- and F-type) stars, there are many known stars with directly measured strong, globally organized magnetic fields, as well as indications of weak and/or small-scale variable fields. However, among the intermediate-mass $γ$ Dor pulsators, there are no known stars with strong surface magnetic fields.
  Aims. The broad goal of this work is to search for evidence of strong, globally organized fields at the surface of $γ$ Dor pulsators.
  Methods. We identified objects consistent with being $γ$ Dor pulsators based on an analysis of space photometry from the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) mission. A spectropolarimetric survey was then conducted on a subset of 47 of these objects, with a precision sufficient to detect dipolar surface magnetic fields down to a threshold of about 10 -- 100 G.
  Results. We detected strong magnetism in three targets. However, upon closer inspection, none of these appear to be genuine $γ$ Dor pulsators. We found no evidence of surface magnetism in any of the remaining 44 objects.
  Conclusions. We conclude that either strong, globally organized magnetic fields and $γ$ Dor pulsation are mutually exclusive, or that such stars are exceedingly rare. A possible explanation is that strong global fields inhibit the excitation mechanism, which prevents $γ$ Dor pulsations from being driven in strongly magnetic intermediate-mass stars. The dipolar surface magnetic field strength upper limits we derive for this sample ($\lesssim$ 50 -- 100 G) provide valuable constraints for surface boundary conditions for asteroseismic models that include magnetism for $γ$ Dor stars.

AI.tldr: This paper searches for strong, globally organized magnetic fields in γ Dor pulsators using TESS photometry and spectropolarimetry of 47 candidates. Three magnetic stars were found, but none were genuine γ Dor pulsators; the remaining 44 showed no evidence of surface magnetism, suggesting strong global fields and γ Dor pulsation are mutually exclusive or extremely rare.
AI.motivation: Intermediate-mass stars can host strong globally organized magnetic fields, but no such fields have been found in γ Dor pulsators. The goal is to search for evidence of strong surface magnetic fields in these pulsating stars to understand the relationship between magnetism and pulsation.
AI.method: γ Dor pulsator candidates were identified from TESS space photometry. A spectropolarimetric survey of 47 objects was conducted with sensitivity to detect dipolar surface magnetic fields down to ~10–100 G.
AI.result: Strong magnetism was detected in three targets, but none were confirmed as genuine γ Dor pulsators. No evidence of surface magnetism was found in the remaining 44 objects.
AI.conclusion: Strong, globally organized magnetic fields and γ Dor pulsation are either mutually exclusive or extremely rare. A possible explanation is that strong global fields inhibit the excitation mechanism needed to drive γ Dor pulsations. The upper limits (~50–100 G) provide constraints for asteroseismic models incorporating magnetism.

title: First and Comprehensive Study of V0757 Pup : $γ-$Doradus Pulsator in Detached Eclipsing Binary
comment: 22 pages, 15 figures, submitted to PASJ. Comments are welcome
summary: Pulsating stars in detached eclipsing binary (EA) systems are known for providing many important physical informations which constrain both stellar structure and evolution theories. To date, fewer than 50 $γ$ Doradus (GDOR) stars have been found in eclipsing binary systems, making them important targets to study \textit{g}-mode pulsation inside the stars. We present a comprehensive physical and pulsational analysis of V0757 Pup (TIC 6939791), a detached eclipsing binary system observed by the TESS mission (Sectors 7, 34, 61, and 88) and followed up with ground-based spectroscopy from the Thai National Telescope. By combining light curve modeling with radial velocities derived from medium-resolution spectra, we determined the fundamental stellar and atmospheric parameters with high precision. The system consists of an F2V primary ($M_1=1.305\pm0.026M_\odot, R_1=1.643\pm0.020R_\odot$) and a G1V secondary ($M_2=0.934\pm0.030M_\odot, R_2=0.941\pm0.079R_\odot$). We performed a detailed frequency analysis of the residual light curves, identifying two dominant independent pulsation frequencies at $f\sim0.79$ c/d and $0.98$ c/d. These frequencies, along with the derived pulsation constant ($Q\sim0.6$ d), confirm the primary component as a $γ$ Doradus pulsator. An analysis of Eclipse Timing Variations (ETV) reveals non detection of third body companions with current available dataset, strengthen by the result of \textit{Gaia} astrometric analysis. Evolutionary modeling indicates the system is $\sim2.2$ Gyr old, with the primary expected to fill its Roche lobe in $\sim1$ Gyr. Additionally, we calculate a distance of $d\approx350$ pc based on orbital and SED modeling, which is in excellent agreement with the \textit{Gaia} DR3 parallax distance.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive photometric and spectroscopic analysis of V0757 Pup, a detached eclipsing binary system containing a γ Doradus pulsator, using TESS light curves and ground-based spectroscopy. The authors derive precise stellar parameters, identify two dominant g-mode pulsation frequencies, rule out third-body companions, and determine the system's evolutionary state and distance.
AI.motivation: Fewer than 50 γ Doradus stars have been found in eclipsing binary systems, yet such systems are crucial for constraining stellar structure and evolution theories since they allow direct determination of stellar masses and radii. V0757 Pup offers a rare opportunity to study g-mode pulsations within a well-characterized eclipsing binary framework.
AI.method: The study combines TESS photometry (Sectors 7, 34, 61, 88) with ground-based medium-resolution spectroscopy from the Thai National Telescope. Light curve modeling, radial velocity analysis, frequency analysis of residual light curves, Eclipse Timing Variation (ETV) analysis, Gaia astrometric analysis, and evolutionary/SED modeling were employed.
AI.result: The system comprises an F2V primary (M=1.305 M☉, R=1.643 R☉) and G1V secondary (M=0.934 M☉, R=0.941 R☉). Two independent pulsation frequencies (~0.79 c/d and 0.98 c/d) with Q~0.6 d confirm the primary as a γ Doradus pulsator. No third-body companions were detected, the system age is ~2.2 Gyr, and the derived distance (~350 pc) agrees excellently with Gaia DR3.
AI.conclusion: V0757 Pup is confirmed as a γ Doradus pulsator in a detached eclipsing binary, providing a well-constrained system for testing stellar structure and evolution models. The primary will fill its Roche lobe in ~1 Gyr, and the system's precise parameters make it a valuable benchmark for future asteroseismic studies.

title: 1.5D investigation of the Hanle effect in the Ca I 4227 line using partial frequency redistribution. Comparison of synthetic Stokes profiles in Bifrost and MURaM-ChE rMHD models
summary: Modeling scattering polarization in the Ca I 4227 Å line is important for diagnosing chromospheric magnetic fields. We investigate the relative influence of formation heights and magnetic fields, through the Hanle effect, on spatially averaged synthetic Stokes profiles using realistic solar atmospheres. We employ 1D vertical columns from 3D radiative magnetohydrodynamic simulations of the solar chromosphere performed with the Bifrost and MURaM-ChE codes, and solve the 1.5D non-local thermodynamic equilibrium polarized radiative transfer equation including partial frequency redistribution and the Hanle effect. The intensity profiles from both simulations agree at line center, while MURaM-ChE exhibits enhanced wing intensity due to deeper, hotter formation regions. The polarization signals form at greater heights in MURaM-ChE than in Bifrost. In the non-magnetic case, Bifrost produces stronger line-core polarization, whereas MURaM-ChE shows enhanced wing polarization. Including the magnetic fields from the simulations results in stronger Hanle depolarization of <Q>/<I> in Bifrost. The distinct thermal and magnetic structures at the corresponding formation heights therefore produce significantly different polarization profiles. In particular, the Hanle signatures suggest that the line-core formation region in MURaM-ChE is less strongly magnetized than that in Bifrost.

AI.tldr: This paper compares synthetic scattering polarization profiles of the Ca I 4227 Å line computed from two different 3D radiative MHD simulations (Bifrost and MURaM-ChE) to investigate how formation heights and magnetic fields (via the Hanle effect) influence spatially averaged Stokes profiles. While both models agree in intensity at line center, they produce significantly different polarization profiles due to distinct thermal and magnetic structures at their respective formation heights, with Bifrost showing stronger line-core polarization and stronger Hanle depolarization.
AI.motivation: Modeling scattering polarization in the Ca I 4227 Å line is important for diagnosing chromospheric magnetic fields, and understanding how model-dependent atmospheric structures influence synthetic polarization profiles is critical for reliable magnetic field inference.
AI.method: The authors employ 1D vertical columns extracted from 3D radiative magnetohydrodynamic simulations (Bifrost and MURaM-ChE) of the solar chromosphere and solve the 1.5D non-LTE polarized radiative transfer equation, including partial frequency redistribution and the Hanle effect, to compute spatially averaged synthetic Stokes I and Q profiles.
AI.result: Intensity profiles agree at line center, but MURaM-ChE shows enhanced wing intensity from deeper, hotter formation regions. Polarization forms at greater heights in MURaM-ChE. In the non-magnetic case, Bifrost produces stronger line-core polarization while MURaM-ChE shows enhanced wing polarization. With magnetic fields included, Bifrost exhibits stronger Hanle depolarization of <Q>/<I>, indicating the line-core formation region in MURaM-ChE is less strongly magnetized.
AI.conclusion: The distinct thermal and magnetic structures at the corresponding formation heights in the two simulations produce significantly different polarization profiles. The Hanle signatures indicate that atmospheric model choice strongly affects inferred chromospheric magnetic fields, with MURaM-ChE having a weaker magnetic field in its line-core formation region than Bifrost.

title: Chemical fingerprints of binary mass transfer in massive stars
comment: Published in Nature Astronomy. Link to the paper: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41550-026-02943-1
summary: The majority of massive stars are born in close binary systems. As stars expand when they age, mass transfer or even a merger with their companion is inevitable. However, most binary interaction products appear as single stars, such that the main evidence of their exciting past is lost. In a comprehensive grid of detailed massive binary evolution models we find systematic trends in chemical surface abundances that allow identifying the past mass gainers. We develop an analytic framework which is independent of specific evolutionary models, to constrain the amount and composition of the accreted material from their observed surface abundances. This yields tight constraints on the uncertain mass transfer physics in massive binary stars and allows us to reconstruct the past evolutionary history of the progenitor binary system. This method, which is shown to also constrain binary mergers (for example, SN 1987A), is applied to some of the best-studied OB stars so far. For γ Columbae, suggested to be an envelope-stripped star, we show that it is a mass gainer instead, whose companion star likely formed a stripped-envelope supernova. Our results highlight surface abundance measurements as a powerful tool to improve our understanding of massive binary systems evolving towards supernovae and compact object binaries.

AI.tldr: The paper presents an analytic framework, independent of specific evolutionary models, that uses chemical surface abundances to identify past mass gainers in massive binary star systems and constrain the amount and composition of accreted material, thereby reconstructing the binary's evolutionary history.
AI.motivation: Most massive stars form in close binaries, but most binary interaction products appear as single stars, losing the primary evidence of their past. There is a need to identify these past interaction products and constrain the uncertain mass transfer physics.
AI.method: A comprehensive grid of detailed massive binary evolution models is used to find systematic trends in chemical surface abundances. An analytic framework independent of specific evolutionary models is developed to constrain the amount and composition of accreted material from observed surface abundances, applicable to both binary mass transfer and mergers.
AI.result: The framework tightly constrains mass transfer physics in massive binaries and is applied to well-studied OB stars, including demonstrating that γ Columbae (previously suggested as envelope-stripped) is in fact a mass gainer whose companion likely formed a stripped-envelope supernova. The method also constrains binary mergers like SN 1987A.
AI.conclusion: Surface abundance measurements are a powerful tool for improving understanding of massive binary systems evolving toward supernovae and compact object binaries, allowing reconstruction of past evolutionary histories of progenitor binary systems.

title: New constraints on the binary system HD 327083 and its gaseous and dusty environments
summary: Binary systems with circumbinary molecular and dust rings are of great interest because they provide insights into the dynamics and evolution of stellar systems and the chemistry of the surrounding material. We aim to elucidate the nature of the B[e] binary system HD 327083 and the physical properties of its circumstellar and circumbinary envelopes. We combined multi-epoch high-spectral resolution optical and near-IR observations with VLTI/MIDI observations and ASAS-3 photometry. The data were analysed to obtain the orbital parameters, study individual members of the system, and derive the properties of the atomic and molecular gas and the dusty components of the complex environment of HD 327083. We improved the orbital solution of HD 327083 and derived a period of P = 107.699 d. Most optical lines display variations in shape and intensity when folded with the orbital motion. We assigned F6 II-III and B1 spectral types respectively to the cool and hot components. A ring of molecular gas revolves around the system and varies with the orbital phase. The MIDI data show a silicate band in absorption at 9.7 micron and indicate that the dust distribution has an elliptical shape, with its inner edge varying with orbital phase between 12.5 and 44 AU. We conclude that the B[e] binary system HD 327083 comprises a B-type massive accreting star, and an F-type companion filling over 60% of its Roche lobe and evolving towards the red supergiant stage. The deformed shape of the F-type star causes a broad minimum in the light curve. The hot companion (26 000 K, log g = 3.0) is hidden by a compact disc and shows a bi-polar outflow. The entire binary system presents an O-rich environment. It is surrounded by warm CO and SiO molecular rings, which are enclosed by an elliptical dust structure. All these components were formed by the evolved donor star during its evolution towards the red supergiant phase.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive multi-wavelength study of the B[e] binary system HD 327083 using optical, near-IR, VLTI/MIDI interferometry, and photometry. The authors refine the orbital period to P = 107.699 d, classify the components as F6 II-III (cool) and B1 (hot) spectral types, and characterize a complex environment comprising a deformed mass-transferring donor star, a compact accretion disc around the hot companion with bi-polar outflow, warm CO and SiO molecular rings, and an elliptical silicate dust ring with an inner edge varying between 12.5 and 44 AU with orbital phase.
AI.motivation: Binary systems with circumbinary molecular and dust rings are of great interest as they provide insight into the dynamics, evolution, and chemistry of stellar systems. The authors aim to elucidate the nature of the B[e] binary system HD 327083 and determine the physical properties of its circumstellar and circumbinary envelopes.
AI.method: The study combines multi-epoch high-spectral-resolution optical and near-IR observations with VLTI/MIDI interferometric observations and ASAS-3 photometry. The data were analyzed to derive orbital parameters, study individual stellar members, and characterize the atomic/molecular gas and dusty components of the system's complex environment.
AI.result: The orbital period was improved to P = 107.699 d. Spectral types of F6 II-III (cool) and B1 (hot) were assigned to the components. Optical lines vary in shape and intensity with orbital phase. MIDI data reveal a 9.7 micron silicate absorption band and an elliptical dust distribution with inner edge varying from 12.5 to 44 AU with orbital phase. The F-type star fills over 60% of its Roche lobe and is evolving toward the red supergiant stage.
AI.conclusion: HD 327083 is a B[e] binary system comprising a B-type massive accreting star and an F-type companion evolving toward the red supergiant phase. The deformed donor star creates a broad light-curve minimum. The hot companion (26,000 K, log g = 3.0) is hidden by a compact disc with a bi-polar outflow. The system presents an O-rich environment surrounded by warm CO and SiO molecular rings enclosed by an elliptical dust structure, all formed by mass transfer from the evolved donor star.

title: Deep MUSE observations of SNR 0509-67.5 reveal a double degenerate merger progenitor
summary: Deep MUSE observations of SNR 0509-67.5 reveal that the coronal [Fe\,\textsc{xiv}] $\mathrmλ$5303 emission line appears with either one or two velocity components across the entire remnant, arising from reverse-shocked ejecta moving toward and away from the observer. A supervised dense neural network classifies each spaxel and fits Gaussian profiles plus a linear function to the observed line emission. We measure a bulk Doppler velocity of $-1000\pm60~~\mathrm{km~s^{-1}}$, interpreted as the line-of-sight component of the primary white dwarf's orbital velocity in a double-degenerate merger. The red- and blue-shifted ejecta map shows a flattened edge along the north-eastern rim, consistent with the companion's shadow, indicating a binary companion was present at explosion. Modelling this feature as a cone anchored at the explosion centre and applying Bayesian inference, we recover the cone's orientation and half-opening angle. We then use the Eggleton Roche-lobe relation to infer properties of the companion. The companion was likely a ${\sim}0.6~\mathrm{M_\odot}$ white dwarf with radius ${\sim}9800$~km and orbital velocity ${\sim}1700~\mathrm{km~s^{-1}}$ at the time of explosion. Together, these results provide a complete dynamical picture of a Type Ia supernova progenitor system whose maximum-light spectrum is independently constrained by light echo observations.

AI.tldr: Using deep MUSE observations of SNR 0509-67.5, the authors analyze the coronal [Fe XIV] λ5303 emission line to map Doppler-shifted ejecta, revealing a line-of-sight bulk velocity of -1000 km/s and a flattened edge in the red/blue-shifted ejecta map suggesting a binary companion's shadow. Bayesian inference on a cone model and the Eggleton Roche-lobe relation infer the companion was a ~0.6 M☉ white dwarf with a ~9800 km radius and ~1700 km/s orbital velocity at explosion, providing a complete dynamical picture of a Type Ia SN progenitor system.
AI.motivation: To determine the progenitor system of the Type Ia supernova SNR 0509-67.5 by observing reverse-shocked ejecta kinematics, identifying whether a binary companion was present at explosion, and characterizing that companion's physical properties.
AI.method: MUSE observations of the coronal [Fe XIV] λ5303 line; a supervised dense neural network classifies each spaxel and fits Gaussian profiles plus a linear function to the emission. A cone model anchored at the explosion center with Bayesian inference recovers the cone's orientation and half-opening angle, and the Eggleton Roche-lobe relation is used to infer companion properties.
AI.result: Bulk Doppler velocity of -1000±60 km/s (line-of-sight component of the primary WD's orbital velocity); a flattened north-eastern rim in the red/blue-shifted ejecta map consistent with a companion's shadow; the companion was likely a ~0.6 M☉ white dwarf with radius ~9800 km and orbital velocity ~1700 km/s at explosion.
AI.conclusion: The results provide a complete dynamical picture of a Type Ia supernova progenitor system, consistent with a double-degenerate merger scenario where the companion is independently constrained by light echo observations of the maximum-light spectrum.

title: Nascent Embedded-protostar Survey in Taurus (NEST) I: Protostellar Multiplicity
summary: We present new ALMA 0.9 mm and VLA 9 mm observations in the Taurus Molecular Cloud (TMC) of 25 protostellar systems, containing 40 protostars, observed at 0.3" (~20 au) resolution. Within separations of 18-10,000 au, the ALMA/VLA-observed Taurus sample has a multiplicity fraction (MF), defined as the fraction of systems with at least one companion, of 0.50 +/- 0.07, and a companion fraction (CF), defined as the average number of companions per system, of 0.58 +/- 0.20. To build a more complete census of protostellar multiplicity in this region, we supplement the observed sample with 24 protostars (12 protostellar systems and 5 additional companions associated with systems we observed) previously identified through archival infrared or ALMA observations. Together, these 64 individual protostars (37 systems) define our Taurus+ sample, for which we measure higher values of 0.53 +/- 0.06 and 0.72 +/- 0.19 for the MF and CF, respectively. These multiplicity statistics in the TMC are notably higher than those reported in the more clustered star-forming regions of Orion and Perseus at the ~3-4 sigma level, suggesting that Taurus may preserve a larger fraction of primordial multiples. The separation distributions in our samples show populations of both close and wide multiples, but a deficit at intermediate separations of 200-300 au. This pattern may suggest two distinct formation pathways: close binaries (<200 au) arising primarily from disk fragmentation, and wide multiples (>1000 au) from core fragmentation.

AI.tldr: The paper presents new ALMA 0.9 mm and VLA 9 mm observations of 25 protostellar systems (40 protostars) in Taurus, finding high multiplicity fractions (MF=0.50, CF=0.58) that increase further when combined with archival data (MF=0.53, CF=0.72). These values are significantly higher than those in Orion and Perseus (~3-4 sigma), and the separation distribution shows a deficit at 200-300 au, suggesting dual formation pathways: disk fragmentation for close binaries (<200 au) and core fragmentation for wide multiples (>1000 au).
AI.motivation: To build a more complete census of protostellar multiplicity in the Taurus Molecular Cloud using high-resolution ALMA/VLA observations, and to compare with other star-forming regions to understand primordial multiplicity and its formation mechanisms.
AI.method: High-resolution ALMA 0.9 mm and VLA 9 mm observations at 0.3" (~20 au) resolution of 25 protostellar systems (40 protostars), supplemented with archival IR/ALMA data for 24 additional protostars, to measure multiplicity and companion fractions and characterize separation distributions.
AI.result: Multiplicity fraction of 0.50±0.07 and companion fraction of 0.58±0.20 for the observed sample; increased to 0.53±0.06 and 0.72±0.19, respectively, for the combined Taurus+ sample of 64 protostars. These are notably higher (~3-4 sigma) than in Orion and Perseus. The separation distribution shows close and wide multiples but a deficit at 200-300 au.
AI.conclusion: Taurus preserves a larger fraction of primordial multiples compared to more clustered regions, and the bimodal separation distribution suggests two distinct formation pathways: disk fragmentation forming close binaries (<200 au) and core fragmentation forming wide multiples (>1000 au), with a deficit at intermediate separations.

title: Hemispheric Asymmetry of Solar Active Regions Arises from a Nested Population
summary: We investigate the longitude--time distribution of NOAA active regions (ARs) during Solar Cycles 22--24 and find statistically significant North--South asymmetry in AR emergence. Using an activity-nest identification algorithm, we show that this asymmetry is concentrated in the subset of ARs that participate in nests. Nest-member ARs exhibit substantially larger hemispheric asymmetry than either the full AR population or the non-nest population, and the asymmetry is largely removed when nest-member ARs are excluded. Monte Carlo tests with randomized longitudes and temporal perturbations show that the observed nesting and asymmetry exceed random expectations, implying that $\sim$6--18\% of ARs participate in a non-random, hemispherically asymmetric nesting component. This asymmetry is associated with temporally offset bursts of activity and distinct longitudinal clustering between the hemispheres, leading to reduced cross-equatorial coherence in the longitude--time distribution of solar ARs. Intervals of enhanced nesting activity and hemispheric asymmetry broadly coincide with enhanced hemispheric quasi-biennial variability and temporal evolution of the large-scale solar magnetic field, suggesting a possible connection between intermediate-timescale dynamo variability and the hemispheric organization of solar activity.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the longitude-time distribution of NOAA active regions during Solar Cycles 22-24, finding significant North-South asymmetry in AR emergence that is concentrated in activity-nest member ARs. Monte Carlo tests show 6-18% of ARs participate in a non-random, hemispherically asymmetric nesting component, linked to temporally offset bursts of activity and reduced cross-equatorial coherence.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether North-South asymmetry in solar active region emergence is associated with activity nests, and to determine whether this asymmetry reflects non-random, physically meaningful organization of solar activity rather than chance fluctuations.
AI.method: Applied an activity-nest identification algorithm to NOAA active region catalog data across Solar Cycles 22-24; performed Monte Carlo tests with randomized longitudes and temporal perturbations to establish statistical significance against random expectations; compared nesting asymmetry across full, nest-member, and non-nest AR populations.
AI.result: Nest-member ARs show substantially larger hemispheric asymmetry than the full or non-nest populations. Observed nesting and asymmetry exceed random expectations, with ~6-18% of ARs in a non-random asymmetric nesting component. The asymmetry correlates with temporally offset bursts, distinct longitudinal clustering, and reduced cross-equatorial coherence, coinciding with enhanced quasi-biennial variability and large-scale magnetic field evolution.
AI.conclusion: There exists a statistically significant, non-random hemispherically asymmetric nesting component in solar AR emergence, which may be connected to intermediate-timescale dynamo variability affecting the hemispheric organization of solar activity.
